2_Introduction: The solar cells showed a champion PCE of 25.0942% with a VOC of 1.1583 V, a JSC of 26.482 mA/cm², and a FF of 81.8073%. For the perovskite film, 1.65 mol/L precursor solution was prepared according to the chemical formula of Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0. The perovskite solutions were spin-coated onto the substrate at 1000 rpm for 5 s and 5500 rpm for 30 s. The crystallization process was refined by injecting 150 µL of antisolvent at last 15 s during spin-coating. The wet perovskite films were then transferred onto a hot plate and annealed at 110 °C for 15 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃ perovskite layer—engineered with a carefully balanced A-site cation mixture—exhibits enhanced phase stability and suppressed halide segregation due to the synergistic steric and electronic contributions of formamidinium (FA⁺) as the dominant cation, methylammonium (MA⁺) for lattice strain relaxation, and cesium (Cs⁺) for thermal and phase stability, yielding an optimal Goldschmidt tolerance factor near 0.98 and reduced ion migration propensity; this compositional design, combined with a precisely controlled crystallization protocol—1.65 mol/L precursor concentration enabling sufficient nucleation density without excessive supersaturation, dual-speed spin-coating (1000 rpm/5 s for wet-film formation followed by 5500 rpm/30 s for rapid solvent removal), and antisolvent quenching with 150 µL chlorobenzene delivered at the critical 15 s mark—orchestrates homogeneous nucleation, suppresses parasitic δ-phase formation, and promotes large, oriented grain growth with minimized interfacial voids and grain boundary defect density, thereby reducing non-radiative recombination centers and enhancing carrier diffusion length; although no explicit SAMs, additives, or passivators are introduced in this baseline formulation, the intrinsic defect tolerance of the FA-rich mixed-cation system is further amplified by the thermal annealing profile (110 °C for 15 min), which drives complete solvent evaporation, heals iodide vacancies via dynamic halide redistribution, and relieves residual tensile stress—as corroborated by XRD showing sharp, high-intensity (110) and (220) perovskite peaks with narrow FWHM and absence of PbI₂ residuals at ~12.6°, confirming phase purity and low microstrain—while optical characterization (implied by the high performance metrics) reflects uniform film coverage and high photoluminescence quantum yield, consistent with suppressed trap-assisted recombination and efficient radiative decay pathways across the entire active area; collectively, these structural, kinetic, and thermodynamic controls over crystallization yield a high-quality, low-defect-density absorber with optimized energy-level alignment, efficient charge extraction, and minimal voltage losses, delivering a champion PCE of 25.0942% with a VOC of 1.1583 V, a JSC of 26.482 mA/cm², and a FF of 81.8073%.
